question: In your multi-agent research system, the document analysis subagent relies on a function named extract_passages, which will soon return a new result format. A wrapper module, doc_access.py, wraps extract_passages in three functions with new names and exports them. Other modules import only those three functions. You need a complete list of the affected code before you edit anything. Which two steps should you take?

options.text: Use Grep across the whole codebase for each name that doc_access.py exports.
options.reason: After the exported names are known, each one must be searched across the codebase, and Grep is the tool that searches file contents.

options.text: Use Grep for each export of doc_access.py only inside the directory that holds doc_access.py, because callers usually sit next to the wrapper module.
options.reason: Each exported name must be searched across the whole codebase, so callers in other directories, such as other subagents, would be missed.

options.text: Use Grep across the whole codebase for only the most widely used export of doc_access.py, and assume the other two exports have the same callers.
options.reason: The trace requires a search for each exported name, because callers of the other two exports can differ and would be missed.

options.text: Use Edit to change extract_passages first, and then treat the runtime errors from the next research run as the complete list of affected callers.
options.reason: Edit is for targeted modifications, not for tracing usage, and one run reaches only some code paths instead of a search for every exported name.

options.text: Read doc_access.py and list every name that it exports, including any aliases for the wrapped function.
options.reason: Tracing usage across a wrapper module starts by identifying all of the names that the wrapper exports.
